answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through thermodynamic dissipation profiling. Nodes monitor heat flux at a server's coolant inlet during execution spikes, tracking dissipation from its operational zenith down to a resting thermal ember. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of provisioning discrete cooling loops and radiators per identity. However, ambient temperature shifts and pump wear can distort thermal curves, occasionally rejecting legitimate nodes.
